law.long_name: Florida Public Records Act (commonly grouped with the Sunshine Law as 'Florida Sunshine')

primary_citation.notes: Issue title says 'FL Sunshine.' In common usage that label conflates two distinct laws: (1) Ch. 119 Public Records Act, which governs records requests; and (2) § 286.011 Sunshine Law, which governs open meetings. For a public-records assistant we treat 'FL Sunshine' as Ch. 119 plus the constitutional records provision in Art. I § 24(a). Flagged for CEO confirmation in open_questions.

constitutional_basis.value: Fla. Const. Art. I, § 24(a) — guarantees the right of access to government records.
constitutional_basis.notes: Art. I § 24(b) covers open meetings (the actual 'Sunshine Law'). § 24(a) covers records and is the constitutional anchor for Ch. 119.

acknowledgment_deadline.value: No fixed numeric deadline; statute requires response in a 'reasonable time' to 'acknowledge' and produce.
acknowledgment_deadline.notes: Florida's records law uniquely does NOT impose a fixed deadline. Case law (Tribune Co. v. Cannella, 458 So. 2d 1075 (Fla. 1984)) construes 'reasonable time' narrowly — limited to time needed to retrieve and examine the record. Surfacing a number to users requires legal review.

substantive_deadline.value: No fixed numeric deadline; 'reasonable time' standard.
substantive_deadline.citation: Fla. Stat. § 119.07(1)(c); Tribune Co. v. Cannella, 458 So. 2d 1075 (Fla. 1984)

extension_rules.value: No statutory extension mechanism; agencies must produce within a reasonable time absent legitimate retrieval/review delay.

constructive_denial.value: Failure to acknowledge or respond within a reasonable time may give rise to a cause of action; constructive denial is largely judicially constructed.

search_fees.value: Agency may charge a 'special service charge' for the labor cost of personnel required to extensively use information technology resources or extensive clerical or supervisory assistance. Routine retrieval is not chargeable.

copy_fees.value: $0.15 per one-sided copy up to 8.5" x 14"; $0.20 for two-sided. Certified copies: $1.00 each. Other media at actual cost.

fee_waiver.value: Statute does not require fee waiver. Agencies may waive at discretion.
fee_waiver.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 119 (absence of mandatory waiver provision)

accepted_methods.notes: Florida is unusual in not requiring a written request; oral requests are permitted. In practice writing is recommended for record-keeping and appeal preservation.

required_identification.value: No identification required. Agency may not require the requester to disclose identity or purpose.

agency_designation.value: Each agency's custodian of public records. AG's office publishes a Government-in-the-Sunshine Manual that aids identification.

value.name: Active criminal investigative information
value.summary: Information compiled in the course of active criminal investigation or intelligence.

value.name: Agency personnel records — partial
value.summary: Home addresses, phone numbers, photos, etc. of specified categories of public employees.

value.name: Security/system plans
value.summary: Building plans, security plans, IT security records.

value.name: Sealed/confidential by other statute
value.summary: Records made confidential or exempt by other statutes.

value.name: Trade secrets / commercial confidential
value.summary: Trade secrets and proprietary business information.

categories.citation: Fla. Stat. § 119.071 (and numerous statute-specific exemptions scattered across the Florida Statutes)
categories.notes: Florida has hundreds of statute-specific public-records exemptions outside Ch. 119. § 119.071 contains the general categorical exemptions. Full enumeration requires assembling exemptions across the entire Florida Statutes.

burden_of_proof.value: Constitutional and statutory presumption of openness; agency must specifically state the statutory basis for any withholding.
burden_of_proof.citation: Fla. Const. Art. I, § 24(a); Fla. Stat. § 119.07(1)(f)

segregability_rule.value: If a portion of a record is exempt, the agency must redact only the exempt portion and produce the remainder.

administrative_path.value: No formal administrative appeal mechanism. Requester may contact the agency head, the Florida AG's Open Government Mediation Program, or pursue judicial relief directly.
administrative_path.citation: Fla. Stat. Ch. 119 (absence of administrative appeal); AG mediation is voluntary.

judicial_path.value: Civil action in circuit court to compel production. Court must set an immediate hearing and give the case priority.

attorneys_fees.value: Court SHALL award reasonable costs and attorney's fees to a substantially prevailing requester if the agency unlawfully refused access. Civil penalties of up to $500 against knowing-violator officials may also be imposed.
attorneys_fees.notes: Pre-suit notice requirement under § 119.12(2) since 2017 amendments — requester must give the agency 5 business days' notice before filing suit, unless the agency has a documented policy to not produce.

requester_eligibility.value: Any person. Florida public-records access is constitutionally guaranteed and not limited by residency or citizenship.
requester_eligibility.citation: Fla. Const. Art. I, § 24(a); Fla. Stat. § 119.01(1)

open_questions.question: Confirm scope: 'FL Sunshine' in the original ticket — should this v0 entry cover only public records (Ch. 119 + Art. I § 24(a)) or also open meetings (§ 286.011 + Art. I § 24(b))? Public-records assistant scope argues for records only; flagging for confirmation.

Florida has no fixed numeric response deadline. What number, if any, should the product surface to users for the 'response deadline' field? Options: (a) state the 'reasonable time' standard with case-law context, (b) adopt a conservative estimate (e.g., '30 days' as commonly cited in advocacy literature) with disclaimer, (c) decline to display a number.

Enumerate all statute-specific public-records exemptions outside Ch. 119. This is a Florida-specific maintenance burden because exemptions are scattered across the Florida Statutes; v0 lists representative § 119.071 categories only.
